articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations today under its counter narcotics and counter terrorism authorities. These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks supporting dangerous activities globally.

The specific individuals and entities targeted in these designations were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement, but such actions typically involve freezing assets and prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in transactions with the designated parties.

These designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to combating international drug trafficking and terrorist financing by targeting key facilitators and their financial infrastructure.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement, ICC Designation, and Burma-Related Removal
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, alongside a new designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the issuance of associated General Licenses.
Additionally, OFAC confirmed the removal of a Burma-related designation, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against certain entities previously targeted in connection with the country.
These actions reflect OFAC's multifaceted approach to sanctions enforcement, combining penalties for violations with targeted designations and removals based on evolving policy considerations.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a new General License pertaining to Russia-related transactions.

General Licenses typically authorize specific categories of transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under sanctions programs, aiming to mitigate unintended consequences or facilitate certain humanitarian or administrative activities.
The details of this new license will be crucial for U.S. persons and entities engaged in activities that may intersect with Russian interests, providing clarity on permissible transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Issues New GL, and Amends Russia GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran, further intensifying pressure on the Iranian regime.
In conjunction with these Iran-related actions, OFAC also issued a new General License specific to Iran, likely to provide carve-outs for certain humanitarian or other permissible activities.
Additionally, an existing Russia-related General License was amended, indicating ongoing adjustments to the U.S. sanctions framework in response to geopolitical developments.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Designations, Updates Others, and Publishes Iran-Related Alert and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several updates to its sanctions lists, including designations removals and updates to existing designations.
Furthermore, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ), providing crucial guidance to the public regarding compliance with Iran sanctions.

These actions reflect OFAC's continuous efforts to refine and clarify its sanctions programs, ensuring they remain effective while also addressing compliance challenges for businesses and individuals.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations under its counter terrorism authorities.

These actions are part of an ongoing effort to disrupt the financial networks of terrorist organizations and their supporters worldwide, aiming to cut off their access to the international financial system.
The specific entities and individuals targeted were not immediately identified, but such designations typically result in asset freezes and prohibitions on transactions involving U.S. persons.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Transnational Criminal Organization, and Issues Determination and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates, alongside a designation targeting a transnational criminal organization.
In conjunction with these actions, OFAC published an Iran-related determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ), providing further clarity on the scope of the sanctions.
These measures aim to disrupt illicit financial activities and networks supporting both the Iranian regime and international criminal enterprises.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter terrorism and transnational criminal organizations.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced the removal of several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics efforts, and Libya, indicating a recalibration of these specific sanctions programs.
These actions demonstrate OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adding new targets while also delisting others based on evolving intelligence and policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced a broad set of designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics, counter terrorism, Iran-related activities, and non-proliferation efforts.
These comprehensive actions aim to disrupt multiple illicit networks simultaneously, reflecting a concerted effort to address diverse threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy.
The designations will result in asset freezes and prohibitions on transactions for the targeted parties, further isolating them from the international financial system.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, Cuba Sanctions Regulations, New and Amended FAQs, and Cuba-Related Alert
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has published significant regulatory amendments, including new Cuba Sanctions Regulations, which implement Executive Order (EO) 14404 of May 1, 2026.
These amendments also include new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and a Cuba-related OFAC Alert, providing updated guidance on transactions involving Cuba.

The new regulations and guidance aim to restrict indirect dealings with entities on the Cuba Restricted List, eliminate the U-turn authorization, and remove group people-to-people and professional-meeting travel authorizations, effective September 30, 2026.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Civil Money Penalty Against American Express National Bank for BSA/AML Deficiencies
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC determined that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations, citing inadequate resources, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and insufficient training.

Deficiencies included a failure to tailor its BSA/AML risk assessment to its business activities, focusing insufficiently on its dominant credit and charge card products, and processing approximately $13 billion in suspected trade-based money laundering activity.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
